class.name: LaserData2D
class.brief_description: What a laser is: its type, size, phases, aim, walls, hits and looks.
class.description: A laser resource for [LaserSpawner2D] (one [LaserVolley2D] per shot, a beam per pattern slot) or [method BulletFactory2D.spawn_laser]. Three types: a [constant LASER_BEAM] stays on its muzzle and reaches [member length] (or the first wall), a [constant LASER_BOLT] is a [member length] segment flying away at [member speed], a [constant LASER_CURVY] laser is a snake whose head flies (tracking, waving) while its body follows the path the head took. Every laser runs the same phases: charging (a warning line, no hits), growing (its width grows), active ([member active_sec], 0 = until ended), fading, finished (pooled). While it hits, each beam queries the physics space along its length every tick: targets on [member collision_mask] get [signal BulletFactory2D.laser_pierce_started] and [signal BulletFactory2D.laser_hit] (repeated every [member hit_interval_sec]), then [signal BulletFactory2D.laser_pierce_ended]; bodies on [member wall_mask] stop or reflect it. The signals fire on the owner spawner, or the factory for factory lasers. Lasers read the resource every tick, so edits reach lasers that are firing. Every accepted change emits [signal Resource.changed]. Pick a [member preset] for a ready-made behavior.

method.name: create_preset
method.description: Returns a new laser with the behavior of [param preset] (see [member preset]).

method.name: get_matching_preset
method.description: Returns the preset whose behavior knobs these knobs match exactly, else [constant PRESET_CUSTOM].

members.member: Seconds of the active phase (full width, hitting). 0 keeps the laser firing until [method LaserVolley2D.end_laser] (or a bolt or curvy laser that is spent). Must be finite and >= 0.
How each beam aims (see [enum LaserAim]). Track and Lock On need targets: [method LaserVolley2D.set_targets], or the spawner's targeting.
The body texture (its first animation, [code]default[/code] when it has one), playing from the growing start. Empty draws a solid body in [member modulate].
How the body frame covers the beam (see [enum BodyMode]).
Tile mode: how fast the tiled body scrolls along the beam, in px/s (positive flows away from the muzzle).
An animation at the muzzle while charging (from the shot on).
Seconds of the charging phase: the warning line shows the whole path, nothing is hit. 0 fires at once. Must be finite and >= 0.
Whether [Area2D] targets (monitorable) are hit.
Whether physics bodies are hit (bodies on [member wall_mask] are walls, never targets).
The physics layers whose bodies and areas the laser hits.
Tints the body along its length (multiplied with [member modulate]): its start at the muzzle (the tail of a bolt), its end at the tip.
Scale of the point animations (charge, muzzle, tip, pierce, wall impact). Must be finite and > 0.
Beams: how fast the beam grows out of its muzzle into its full length, in px/s (the warning line already shows the whole path). 0 = full length at once. Must be finite and >= 0.
Seconds of the fading phase: the width shrinks to 0, nothing is hit. Must be finite and >= 0.

Whether the muzzles ride their spawner (its moves, spin and teleports) or anchor; off, a beam stays where it was fired. Bolts and curvy lasers leave the muzzle when they launch. The spawner's [member PatternSpawner2D.spawn_position_offset] rides on top of the spun muzzles (Global: a world vector, Local: in the generator's frame), like the bullets' offset. While the spawner is outside the scene tree (a reparent across frames) the beams hold their pose and ride it again once it is back; a freed spawner ends the follow and every beam stays where it is.
Seconds of the growing phase: the width grows from 0 to [member width]. It hits while growing when [member hit_while_growing] is on. Must be finite and >= 0.

0 (default) sends one [signal BulletFactory2D.laser_hit] per contact (when it starts). > 0 repeats it every this many seconds while the target stays in the beam (damage ticks); after a hitch the next hit simply comes, never a burst of missed ones.
Whether the growing phase already hits (default on). Off, only the active phase hits.
Track and Lock On: whether the beam keeps following its target while active. Off, it aims while charging and growing, then holds that direction ("charge, lock, fire").
The beam's length (a beam reaching out of its muzzle, a bolt's segment, a curvy laser's body), in px. Must be finite and > 0.
The canvas material of the laser (for example a [CanvasItemMaterial] with additive blending, or a [ShaderMaterial]).
The most targets one physics query of a beam segment reports (1 to 4096). Raise it when more targets than this can stand in one beam.
The laser's color (multiplied with its textures and [member color_ramp]). Must be finite.
An animation at the muzzle of a beam while it fires (from the growing start).
An animation at every target the beam pierces (from that contact's start, at the target projected onto the beam).

0 (default): passes through every target. A beam with N hits its N nearest targets and stops at the last one (the drawn and damaging length is cut there). A bolt or curvy laser hits N targets over its flight, then it is spent (gone).
Editor only (never saved): picking a preset writes the behavior knobs (type, size, phases, aim, sweep, walls, pierce, hit interval), never the looks. Shows the preset the knobs match, else Custom.
How many walls a beam (or a bolt or curvy head) reflects off before the next wall stops it. Each one is a ray per tick. 0 to 256.
Bolts and curvy lasers: how fast the head flies, in px/s. Must be finite and >= 0.
Beams: 0 keeps the sweep turning; > 0 swings it back and forth inside this arc around its aim.
Beams: how fast the beam turns around its muzzle, in degrees per second (negative turns the other way). 0 = no sweep.
An animation at the tip of the beam (the head of a bolt or curvy laser).
Track (and tracking bolt and curvy heads): how fast it turns toward its target, in degrees per second. 0 snaps onto it.
The kind of laser (see [enum LaserType]).
An animation where the beam meets a wall (where it stops and where it reflects), from the moment it got blocked.
The physics layers whose bodies are walls: a beam stops at the first one (or reflects, see [member reflections]) and never counts it as a target. 0 = passes through walls.
The color of the charging warning line.
The width of the charging warning line, in px (0 = no warning line).
Curvy lasers: how far the head waves sideways, in px (0 = flies straight or tracks).
Curvy lasers: waves per second.
The full width of the beam, drawn and hitting, in px. Must be finite and > 0.
The laser's draw order (-4096 to 4096).

constants.constant: A beam fixed at its muzzle, reaching [member length] (or the first wall).
A [member length] segment flying away at [member speed] (a fast "laser shot").
A snake: the head flies (and tracks or waves), the body follows the path it took.
Each beam points along its pattern slot (plus the sweep).
Each beam turns toward its target at [member turn_rate_degrees].
Each beam ends right on its target (its length is the distance, capped at [member length]).
One body frame stretched over the whole beam.
The body frame repeats every texture width (and scrolls with [member body_scroll_speed]).
Fires at once and hits on its first tick, for half a second.
A one-second warning, then a beam swinging through 90 degrees.
Grows out of the muzzle and stops at walls on layer 1.
Like the wall beam, reflecting off three walls.
A short fast segment that stops at the first target it hits.
A curvy laser chasing its target.
Warns, then ends right on its target.
